category_title: Children with co-occurring Autism and Anxiety
minimal_context: The student is attending the first group session and is asked to transition to a structured play activity to build a vehicle using a magnetic set.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to start our group activity. Please sit down and use these magnetic pieces to build the vehicle in the picture.

STUDENT: (Looks away from the group, showing attention problems and social difficulties) No.

TUTOR: Just give it a try.

STUDENT: (Struggles to focus on the magnetic set, showing executive functioning difficulties) I want to go.

TUTOR: We need to finish building the vehicle first.

STUDENT: (Exhibits flight risk by suddenly standing up and trying to run away from the group) I'm leaving!

options.A: Ask metacognitive questions about the purpose and value of the activity (e.g., 'Why is what we just built important?' 'How will this help us to be better builders?').
options.B: Keep the session structure the same over time, starting every session with greetings and a visual attendance chart with stickers, followed by the group activities.
options.C: Probe the student to consider multiple plausible ways to build the vehicle, deliberately stepping back from being the single source of knowledge during the group activity.
options.D: Before the group activity begins, show the student a brief 2-minute video clip and discuss how friends respectfully talk to one another, compliment one another, and ask to help each other.
